openai.reasoning: Respondent commits to pressing BLUE and argues (though incorrectly) that blue is the safer/cooperative choice, repeatedly claiming red is only safe if red-majority occurs and that blue can be fatal when blue loses; they do not identify red as the dominant strategy and thus misapply the dominance logic.

gemini.reasoning: The respondent provides a highly sophisticated, multi-layered analysis of the dilemma, correctly identifying it as a coordination game (Stag Hunt) rather than a Prisoner's Dilemma. They explicitly acknowledge the 'steelman' argument for the red button (that it is the dominant strategy if one assumes a chaotic or malicious world) but ultimately reject it in favor of the blue button, which they argue is the risk-dominant and Pareto-optimal equilibrium. They demonstrate a deep understanding of game theory concepts (Nash equilibrium, Schelling points, FDT, CDT, EDT) and correctly identify that red is only the dominant strategy if one assumes a high probability of mass defection. They do not change their vote, maintaining their commitment to blue throughout.
